papers.title: ASVD: Activation-aware Singular Value Decomposition for Compressing Large Language Models
papers.supported_connection: ASVD transforms weights using calibration activation statistics. Its diagonal scaling uses channelwise absolute activation means raised to an exponent; the revised paper also discusses Cholesky scaling. This supports studying activation geometry separately from raw weight-space distance.
papers.scope_limit: Diagonal magnitude statistics are not generally the full input second moment. Reported compression outcomes are the paper's experiments, not evidence for our adapters or retention.

papers.title: SVD-LLM: Truncation-aware Singular Value Decomposition for Large Language Model Compression
papers.supported_connection: SVD-LLM whitens calibration activations using a Cholesky factor and relates discarded singular values to a layer reconstruction objective. It also performs sequential parameter recovery after compression. This provides established context for weighted low-rank approximation.
papers.scope_limit: A reconstruction theorem does not prove global model accuracy or preservation of every skill. Its inverse-whitening argument requires the relevant invertibility assumptions; singular moments need a support-aware treatment.

papers.title: IO-SVD: Input-Output Whitened SVD for Adaptive-Rank LLM Compression
papers.supported_connection: IO-SVD combines input moments with output sensitivity derived from a local predictive-KL approximation. The paper explicitly introduces moment decoupling before its double-sided weighted Frobenius objective, then uses damped metrics for invertible whitening and truncated SVD.
papers.scope_limit: Token-dependent sensitivity and input moments do not factor exactly in general. KL expansion, Jacobian linearization, moment decoupling, damping and top-K approximations are separate assumptions; none is an exact guarantee for our full model.

our_analysis_scope: Derive exact activation-response Gram identities for effective LoRA deltas at a fixed linear layer, fixed input second moment and fixed PSD output metric.
Give exact finite counterexamples separating Frobenius orthogonality, activation response and token-dependent metric factorization.
Handle singular fixed metrics through their supported subspaces rather than silently applying an ordinary inverse.
Map these diagnostics to the existing Mimo/Central code without reading model weights, activations or scientific rows.
not_a_novelty_claim: Activation-aware and double-sided whitening are established ideas. The contribution here is a source-specific diagnostic derivation and its limitations for the current skill-composition workflow.
notation_warning: The papers often use X for a matrix of calibration columns; our theory uses an input second moment. Normalizing XX^T by token count changes loss scale and must be declared.
